claims.text: Random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr has high chemical disorder and severe lattice distortion.
Chemical short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr produces HfTi and TiZr binary clusters with B2-like order.
Thermal annealing or Monte Carlo simulation can induce chemical short-range order.
The proposed effect applies below the order-disorder transition, where the B2-like short-range order remains stable.
The comparison is at ambient pressure and fixed equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr composition.
Ordering the binary clusters reduces local lattice distortion relative to the random solid solution.
The ordered clusters form a percolating network.
Ordering reduces the variance of local atomic-size and bonding environments.
Reduced local lattice distortion lowers the scattering rate or scattering cross-section of high-frequency phonons.
Percolating ordered clusters provide continuous low-scattering pathways that extend phonon mean free paths.
Formation of a sufficiently ordered, percolating cluster network increases lattice thermal conductivity relative to random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr.
Random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr has low lattice thermal conductivity because severe lattice distortion strongly scatters phonons.
Ordering reduces broadening of the high-frequency phonon density of states.
Atomic displacement amplitudes or Debye-Waller factors decrease within the ordered clusters.
A conductivity increase requires both cluster percolation and sufficient ordering to reduce lattice distortion.
Incomplete ordering or isolated clusters decrease conductivity because cluster boundaries add phonon scattering.
The exact percolation threshold of HfTi and TiZr clusters in HfNbTaTiZr is uncertain.
The balance between distortion reduction and cluster-boundary scattering varies with annealing time and temperature.
Electronic thermal conductivity is negligible for the proposed comparison.

contradictions.description: The boundary explicitly allows conductivity to decrease when ordering is incomplete or clusters remain isolated, whereas the falsification experiment states broadly that a conductivity decrease upon ordering falsifies the hypothesis. A decrease is only decisive after verifying that the stipulated ordering and percolation conditions were achieved.
